1: # HW5 — From Ratings to Recommendations (Matrix Factorization)
2: 
3: **Course**: LLM4Rec, HSE University
4: **Instructor**: Seungmin Jin (sedzhin@hse.ru)
5: **Repository**: https://github.com/dryjins/RecSys-LLMs/tree/main/week5
6: **Task type**: Assignment (individual)
7: 
8: ---
9: 
10: ## 1. Learning goals
11: 
12: By the end of this assignment you should be able to:
13: 
14: - Turn a sparse rating log into a **user–movie rating matrix** and explain why an
15:   unobserved rating is **missing data, not a zero**.
16: - Split ratings **per user, by timestamp**, into an **80% train / 10% validation /
17:   10% test** protocol that mimics "predict the future from the past".
18: - Implement **matrix factorization** with **16-dimensional** user and movie
19:   vectors and a **dot-product** prediction rule.
20: - Train the factors with **batched tensor operations in TensorFlow.js**, using
21:   an optimizer (`tf.train.adam` / `tf.train.sgd`) instead of hand-written
22:   per-rating JavaScript loops.
23: - Select a checkpoint by **validation RMSE** and report **test RMSE** against a
24:   **training-set mean-rating baseline**.
25: - Generate **Top-10 recommendation lists** that exclude movies the user already
26:   rated in training or validation.
27: - Evaluate retrieval with **Recall@10**, treating test ratings **>= 4.0** as
28:   relevant, and report the evaluation **exclusions** that make the number
29:   interpretable.
30: - Reason about whether a recommender helps users **discover** new movies or mainly
31:   **repeats** their existing preferences, and what that means for a streaming
32:   platform.
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 2. Run instructions
37: 
38: Serve the folder over HTTP and open `week5/index.html` in a modern browser:
39: 
40: ```bash
41: cd week5
42: python3 -m http.server 8000
43: # then open http://localhost:8000/
44: ```
45: 
46: The page needs an **HTTP server** (because `data.js` uses `fetch()` to read
47: `u.data` and `u.item`) and **network access** on first load (the browser fetches
48: the TensorFlow.js CDN script). It also runs on static hosting such as GitHub
49: Pages, which serves files over HTTP.
50: 
51: Keep `week5/u.data`, `week5/u.item`, `week5/data.js`, `week5/style.css`, and
52: `week5/script.js` next to `index.html`. Press **Run tests** to execute the
53: self-checks, fill in the six `TODO(hw5)` stubs, then press **Train**,
54: **Recommend Top-10**, and **Evaluate Recall@10**. The backend that TensorFlow.js
55: selected is shown in the **TensorFlow.js status** panel (`#tf-status`).
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 3. Dataset provenance
60: 
61: - **Source**: MovieLens 100k (GroupLens / University of Minnesota).
62:   - Dataset page: `https://grouplens.org/datasets/movielens/100k/`
63: - **Files used** (byte-identical to Week 2 and Week 3, so the **algorithm** is the
64:   only variable between the assignments):
65:   - `u.data` — **100,000 ratings**, tab-separated
66:     `userId | movieId | rating | timestamp`.
67:   - `u.item` — **1,682 movies**, pipe-separated
68:     `id | title | release | video | url | 18 genre flags`.
69: - **Shapes in this dataset**: **943 users**, **1,682 movies**, **100,000 ratings**.
70:   The highest user id is **943** and the highest movie id is **1,682**, so the
71:   dense rating matrix is `(943 + 1) x (1682 + 1)`.
72: - **Timestamps**: every rating in `u.data` carries a Unix timestamp; the split in
73:   `data.js` sorts each user's ratings by ascending timestamp (ties broken by
74:   `movieId`).
75: - **Citation** (as required by the source): F. Maxwell Harper and Joseph A.
76:   Konstan, "The MovieLens Datasets: History and Context", *ACM Transactions on
77:   Interactive Intelligent Systems*, 2015.
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 4. Tensors and GPU acceleration
82: 
83: ### 4.1 What TensorFlow.js is
84: 
85: **TensorFlow.js** is a JavaScript library for **tensor computation and automatic
86: differentiation**: tensors are multi-dimensional arrays, operations over them are
87: expressed as library calls, and each operation records enough information to
88: compute gradients automatically. It runs entirely **in the browser** and can use
89: the **WebGL** backend to execute tensor operations on the **GPU**, falling back
90: to the pure-JavaScript **CPU** backend when WebGL is unavailable.
91: 
92: `week5/index.html` already loads the runtime from a CDN before the page scripts:
93: 
94: ```html
95: <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tensorflow/tfjs@4.22.0/dist/tf.min.js"></script>
96: <script src="data.js"></script>
97: <script src="script.js"></script>
98: ```
99: 
100: Because this is a plain (classic) script load, TensorFlow.js exposes a global
101: **`tf`** object that `week5/script.js` can use directly — no module import is
102: needed.
103: 
104: ### 4.2 Use TensorFlow.js (required)
105: 
106: Implement the **matrix-factorization training** and the **batched scoring** with
107: TensorFlow.js tensor operations rather than hand-written JavaScript loops over
108: rating arrays. TensorFlow.js is the GPU-accelerated path expected for this
109: assignment. The six stubs expect these APIs:
110: 
111: | Purpose | API |
112: |---|---|
113: | Learnable factor matrices | `tf.variable` |
114: | Small random initialization | `tf.randomNormal(shape, mean, std)` |
115: | Gather rows for a batch of user/movie ids | `tf.gather` |
116: | Score many (user, movie) pairs at once | `tf.matMul` (and element-wise `mul` / `sum`) |
117: | Loss for a training batch | `tf.losses.meanSquaredError` |
118: | Optimizer and in-place update | `tf.train.adam` / `tf.train.sgd` + `optimizer.minimize` |
119: | Top-K over all item scores | `tf.topk` |
120: | Automatic release of intermediate tensors | `tf.tidy` |
121: 
122: The result is the same algorithm as a handwritten implementation, but each
123: mini-batch is one tensor operation executed on the GPU where possible.
124: 
125: ### 4.3 Practical points
126: 
127: - **Select the backend and report it.** `initTf()` in `script.js` prefers WebGL,
128:   falls back to CPU, and writes the chosen backend into `#tf-status` via
129:   `tf.getBackend()`. State the printed backend in your report: if it says `cpu`,
130:   the GPU path was not used and your timings are host-CPU numbers.
131: - **Await readiness once.** Call `await tf.ready()` before the first training
132:   step so the backend is fully initialized (the provided `initTf()` already does
133:   this).
134: - **Manage memory.** Wrap per-step work in `tf.tidy` and **dispose** long-lived
135:   tensors you no longer need. TensorFlow.js tensors live outside the JavaScript
136:   heap; undisposed tensors leak GPU memory, especially inside an epoch loop.
137:   Re-initializing the model (repeated **Train** clicks) must also dispose the
138:   previous `tf.Variable`s.
139: - **The first CDN load needs network access.** On a machine without network the
140:   `tf` global is undefined; the page shows a clear message instead of throwing
141:   (see `initTf()`).
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 5. Required student work
146: 
147: ### 5.1 Implementation Task
148: 
149: - **Dataset**: MovieLens. Use `userId` and `movieId` to identify users and movies;
150:   use `title` and `genres` to describe movies. Reuse the same `u.data` / `u.item`
151:   files as Week 2 and Week 3.
152: - **Data preparation**: build a user–movie rating matrix. Treat missing ratings as
153:   **unobserved, not zeros**.
154: - **Data splitting**: sort each user's ratings by **timestamp** and use
155:   **80% train / 10% validation / 10% test** (provided by `data.js`).
156: - **Matrix factorization**: implement JavaScript matrix factorization with
157:   **16-dimensional** user and movie vectors; the predicted rating is their
158:   **dot product**.
159: - **Model evaluation**: select the checkpoint using **validation RMSE**. Compare
160:   **test RMSE** against a **training-set mean-rating baseline**.
161: - **Recommendation**: generate **Top-10** lists for **two users**. Show movie
162:   titles and scores, and **exclude movies rated in training or validation**.
163: - **Retrieval evaluation**: treat test ratings **>= 4.0** as relevant and report
164:   **Recall@10** using **training-set movies as candidates**. Report the
165:   **evaluation exclusions** for unseen ids (relevant test movies absent from the
166:   training pool) and for users without an eligible relevant test movie.
167: 
168: You implement **six stubs**, each marked `TODO(hw5)`, in `week5/script.js`:
169: `initializeFactors`, `trainMF`, `predictRating`, `selectBestCheckpoint`,
170: `recommendTopK`, and `recallAtK`.
171: 
172: ### 5.2 Business & Algorithmic Analysis (exactly ONE question)
173: 
174: Answer **only** the following question (in the course report, using numbers and
175: titles produced by your own code):
176: 
177: **Familiar Choices vs. New Discoveries.** Do your recommendations help users
178: **discover** movies, or do they mainly **repeat** their existing preferences?
179: Compare two users' Top-10 lists with their past ratings. Use specific movies or
180: genres to explain what the lists are worth to a streaming platform.
181: 
182: ---
183: 
184: ## 6. Definitions
185: 
186: Let a rating be `r(u, i)`, the rating user `u` gave movie `i`.
187: 
188: The model stores a **global training mean** `mu` and two **16-dimensional** factor
189: vectors per id: `p_u` for user `u` and `q_i` for movie `i`. The predicted rating is
190: 
191: ```
192: r_hat(u, i) = mu + p_u . q_i
193: ```
194: 
195: where `.` is the dot product. The result is clamped to `[1, 5]`.
196: 
197: The dense factor matrices are indexed by the **raw** user and movie ids:
198: 
199: - `userFactors`: shape `[numUsers + 1, 16]` = `[944, 16]`, row index = `userId`.
200: - `itemFactors`: shape `[maxMovieId + 1, 16]` = `[1683, 16]`, row index = `movieId`.
201: - `globalMean`: the mean rating over the **training** split.
202: 
203: **RMSE** (root-mean-square error) over a split of `N` ratings:
204: 
205: ```
206: RMSE = sqrt( (1 / N) * SUM_over_ratings ( r_hat(u, i) - r(u, i) )^2 )
207: ```
208: 
209: **Mean-rating baseline**: predict the training-set mean `mu` for every pair and
210: compute the RMSE on the same split. It is the number your factorization must beat.
211: The provided `computeBaselineRMSE` implements it.
212: 
213: **Recall@K**: with **relevant** = test ratings with `rating >= 4.0` and
214: **candidates** = the set of movie ids appearing anywhere in the training split,
215: for each evaluable user
216: 
217: ```
218: recall_u = ( number of that user's relevant candidate movies in the Top-K list ) / ( number of that user's relevant candidate movies )
219: ```
220: 
221: and `Recall@K` is the **mean of `recall_u` over the evaluable users**. Movies
222: rated in training or validation are excluded from a user's list, so a relevant
223: test movie that the user already rated in training cannot be recommended (and is
224: counted in the **unseen ids** exclusion report).
225: 
226: ---
227: 
228: ## 7. Implementation & analysis tasks
229: 
230: 1. Read `week5/script.js` and identify the six `TODO(hw5)` stubs:
231:    `predictRating`, `initializeFactors`, `trainMF`, `selectBestCheckpoint`,
232:    `recommendTopK`, and `recallAtK`. The rest of the file (TensorFlow.js
233:    bootstrap, `computeRMSEFor`, `computeBaselineRMSE`, formatting helpers, all DOM
234:    renderers, the hyper-parameter reader, the pipeline wrapper, and the test
235:    harness) is scaffolding and should be left as-is.
236: 2. Run the page, press **Run tests**, and record the baseline counts. With the
237:    stubs untouched the harness reports **4 passed / 0 failed / 7 pending** (the
238:    provided helpers pass; the seven stub-backed checks are reported as PENDING
239:    rather than FAIL). After a correct implementation all **11** checks pass.
240: 3. Implement the six stubs with TensorFlow.js tensor operations, following the
241:    API guide in §4.2 and the per-stub contract notes in the code.
242: 4. Press **Train** with the default hyper-parameters and report the **validation
243:    RMSE** at the selected checkpoint and the **test RMSE** of that checkpoint.
244:    Compare the test RMSE with the **training-set mean-rating baseline** from
245:    `computeBaselineRMSE(testSet)` and state whether the factorization beats it.
246: 5. Generate the **Top-10** list for **two users** and record each movie's **title**
247:    and **score**. Confirm that none of the listed movies was rated by that user in
248:    training or validation.
249: 6. Evaluate **Recall@10** on the test split and report the overall recall together
250:    with the **exclusions**: the number of unseen relevant test items and the
251:    number of users without a relevant candidate.
252: 7. Answer the single **§5.2** analysis question, comparing the two users' Top-10
253:    lists with their past ratings and citing specific movies or genres.
254: 8. Verify every citation you use (paper, URL, authors, year) before submitting,
255:    and export the unmodified `session.json` for the report (see §8).
256: 
257: ---
258: 
259: ## 8. Submission instructions
260: 
261: Submit the **modified `week5/` directory** (or your own repository) containing the
262: files below, plus the course report.
263: 
264: | File | Role |
265: |---|---|
266: | `week5/script.js` | your implementation of the six `TODO(hw5)` stubs |
267: | `week5/data.js` | data layer (provided, do not modify) |
268: | `week5/index.html` | page structure (provided, do not modify) |
269: | `week5/style.css` | styling (provided, do not modify) |
270: | `week5/readme.md` | this file |
271: 
272: Plus:
273: 
274: - `report.pdf` — IEEE-aligned report per the course homework guidelines
275:   (`docs/homework-guidelines/guidelines.md`), answering §5.2.
276: - `session.json` — the **unmodified** export from your AI tool
277:   (`opencode export <sessionID>`).
278: 
279: - **No Jupyter notebook** (`.ipynb`) is part of this deliverable.
280: - **No separate memo** is required; the analysis belongs in the report.
281: - **Late submissions are not accepted.**
282: 
283: ---
284: 
285: ## 9. Grading criteria
286: 
287: Grading follows the course homework guidelines, **§8 — Rubric Criteria in Detail**
288: (`docs/homework-guidelines/guidelines.md`). The two criteria are **binary** (0 or
289: 1) and combine into a per-assignment score of **0, 1, or 2**:
290: 
291: - **c1 — Problem & References.** Clear problem statement; all references valid;
292:   attribution accurate. A hallucinated citation, a broken reference URL, or a
293:   fabricated author/year is a **Gate 0** failure of c1.
294: - **c2 — Solution & Evidence.** The solution works (the page runs and the numbers
295:   shown match the code's own output); the reasoning is accurate; and verification
296:   is cited (for example a hand-computed RMSE on one pair, a re-run, a source read
297:   beyond the abstract, or a cross-check of a reported number against the code).
298: 
299: Read **§10** of the same guidelines for the **Gate 0** failure modes that apply
300: most directly here:
301: 
302: - a **hallucinated citation** (a paper or URL that does not exist);
303: - **fabricated verification** — claiming you hand-computed or re-ran something you
304:   did not;
305: - a **broken solution** — the page does not run, or the numbers shown do not match
306:   the code's own output;
307: - a **hallucinated API call** — reporting use of a TensorFlow.js function that
308:   does not exist or is not actually used.
309: 
310: If you cannot verify a critical output, say so honestly in the report's AI-usage
311: section rather than claiming verification you did not perform.
312: 
313: ---

- **Matrix factorization**: implement JavaScript matrix factorization with
  **16-dimensional** user and movie vectors; the predicted rating is their
  **dot product**.
- **Model evaluation**: select the checkpoint using **validation RMSE**. Compare
  **test RMSE** against a **training-set mean-rating baseline**.
- **Recommendation**: generate **Top-10** lists for **two users**. Show movie
  titles and scores, and **exclude movies rated in training or validation**.
- **Retrieval evaluation**: treat test ratings **>= 4.0** as relevant and report
  **Recall@10** using **training-set movies as candidates**. Report the
  **evaluation exclusions** for unseen ids (relevant test movies absent from the
  training pool) and for users without an eligible relevant test movie.

You implement **six stubs**, each marked `TODO(hw5)`, in `week5/script.js`:
`initializeFactors`, `trainMF`, `predictRating`, `selectBestCheckpoint`,
`recommendTopK`, and `recallAtK`.

### 5.2 Business & Algorithmic Analysis (exactly ONE question)

Answer **only** the following question (in the course report, using numbers and
titles produced by your own code):

**Familiar Choices vs. New Discoveries.** Do your recommendations help users
**discover** movies, or do they mainly **repeat** their existing preferences?
Compare two users' Top-10 lists with their past ratings. Use specific movies or
genres to explain what the lists are worth to a streaming platform.

---

## 6. Definitions

Let a rating be `r(u, i)`, the rating user `u` gave movie `i`.

The model stores a **global training mean** `mu` and two **16-dimensional** factor
vectors per id: `p_u` for user `u` and `q_i` for movie `i`. The predicted rating is

```
r_hat(u, i) = mu + p_u . q_i
```

where `.` is the dot product. The result is clamped to `[1, 5]`.

The dense factor matrices are indexed by the **raw** user and movie ids:

- `userFactors`: shape `[numUsers + 1, 16]` = `[944, 16]`, row index = `userId`.
- `itemFactors`: shape `[maxMovieId + 1, 16]` = `[1683, 16]`, row index = `movieId`.
- `globalMean`: the mean rating over the **training** split.

**RMSE** (root-mean-square error) over a split of `N` ratings:

```
RMSE = sqrt( (1 / N) * SUM_over_ratings ( r_hat(u, i) - r(u, i) )^2 )
```

**Mean-rating baseline**: predict the training-set mean `mu` for every pair and
compute the RMSE on the same split. It is the number your factorization must beat.
The provided `computeBaselineRMSE` implements it.

**Recall@K**: with **relevant** = test ratings with `rating >= 4.0` and
**candidates** = the set of movie ids appearing anywhere in the training split,
for each evaluable user

```
recall_u = ( number of that user's relevant candidate movies in the Top-K list ) / ( number of that user's relevant candidate movies )
```

and `Recall@K` is the **mean of `recall_u` over the evaluable users**. Movies
rated in training or validation are excluded from a user's list, so a relevant
test movie that the user already rated in training cannot be recommended (and is
counted in the **unseen ids** exclusion report).

1: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
2: // week5/data.js — MovieLens 100k data layer (classic <script>, no modules)
3: //
4: // Loads u.item (movies) and u.data (ratings), builds a sparse-friendly
5: // rating matrix, and splits every user's ratings chronologically 80/10/10.
6: //
7: // Genre alignment note (fixes the Week-2 off-by-one):
8: //   A u.item row has 24 '|'-separated fields:
9: //     0 id | 1 title | 2 release | 3 video | 4 url | 5 unknown |
10: //     6 Action | 7 Adventure | ... | 23 Western
11: //   Field index 5 is the legacy 19th genre flag "unknown", NOT the first real
12: //   genre. The 18 real flags therefore live at indices 6..23, so we read them
13: //   with fields.slice(6, 24) and pair them with the 18-name `genreNames`
14: //   list below. (The earlier fields.slice(5, 24) + 18 names pairing was off
15: //   by one.)
16: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
17: 
18: // Global variables for storing movie and rating data
19: let movies = [];          // [{ id, title, genres: string[] }]
20: let ratings = [];         // [{ userId, movieId, rating, timestamp }]
21: 
22: // Collaborative filtering structures (populated by buildRatingMatrix)
23: let numUsers = 0;         // highest user id found in u.data
24: let numMovies = 0;        // number of parsed movies
25: let ratingMatrix = null;  // (numUsers + 1) x (maxMovieId + 1); 0 = unobserved
26: 
27: // Genre names for the 18 real flags (u.item field indices 6..23)
28: const genreNames = [
29:     "Action", "Adventure", "Animation", "Children's", "Comedy",
30:     "Crime", "Documentary", "Drama", "Fantasy", "Film-Noir",
31:     "Horror", "Musical", "Mystery", "Romance", "Sci-Fi",
32:     "Thriller", "War", "Western"
33: ];
34: 
35: // Users skipped while splitting (e.g. too few ratings), collected by
36: // splitByTimestamp() for reporting.
37: let SPLIT_EXCLUSIONS = [];
38: 
39: // Primary function to load data from files
40: async function loadData() {
41:     try {
42:         // Load and parse movie data
43:         const moviesResponse = await fetch('u.item');
44:         if (!moviesResponse.ok) {
45:             throw new Error(`Failed to load movie data: ${moviesResponse.status}`);
46:         }
47:         const moviesText = await moviesResponse.text();
48:         parseItemData(moviesText);
49: 
50:         // Load and parse rating data
51:         const ratingsResponse = await fetch('u.data');
52:         if (!ratingsResponse.ok) {
53:             throw new Error(`Failed to load rating data: ${ratingsResponse.status}`);
54:         }
55:         const ratingsText = await ratingsResponse.text();
56:         parseRatingData(ratingsText);
57: 
58:         // Derive matrix dimensions, then build the rating matrix
59:         numUsers = ratings.reduce((max, r) => Math.max(max, r.userId), 0);
60:         numMovies = movies.length;
61:         buildRatingMatrix();
62:     } catch (error) {
63:         console.error('Error loading data:', error);
64:         const errorTarget = document.getElementById('result');
65:         if (errorTarget) {
66:             errorTarget.textContent =
67:                 `Error: ${error.message}. Please make sure u.item and u.data are in the correct location.`;
68:             errorTarget.className = 'error';
69:         }
70:         throw error; // Re-throw so the page script can handle the error
71:     }
72: }
73: 
74: // Parse movie data from u.item format: "id|title|release|video|url|g0|...|g18"
75: // genreNames has 18 entries, matched against the real flags at indices 6..23.
76: function parseItemData(text) {
77:     const lines = text.split('\n');
78: 
79:     for (const line of lines) {
80:         if (line.trim() === '') continue;
81: 
82:         const fields = line.split('|');
83:         if (fields.length < 24) continue; // Skip malformed rows
84: 
85:         const id = parseInt(fields[0]);
86:         const title = fields[1];
87: 
88:         // Read the 18 real genre flags (index 5 is the 'unknown' placeholder)
89:         const genreValues = fields.slice(6, 24).map(value => parseInt(value));
90:         const genres = genreNames.filter((_, index) => genreValues[index] === 1);
91: 
92:         movies.push({ id, title, genres });
93:     }
94: }
95: 
96: // Parse rating data from u.data format: "userId\tmovieId\trating\ttimestamp"
97: function parseRatingData(text) {
98:     const lines = text.split('\n');
99: 
100:     for (const line of lines) {
101:         if (line.trim() === '') continue;
102: 
103:         const fields = line.split('\t');
104:         if (fields.length < 4) continue; // Skip malformed rows
105: 
106:         const userId = parseInt(fields[0]);
107:         const movieId = parseInt(fields[1]);
108:         const rating = parseFloat(fields[2]);
109:         const timestamp = parseInt(fields[3]);
110: 
111:         ratings.push({ userId, movieId, rating, timestamp });
112:     }
113: }
114: 
115: // Build the sparse-friendly rating matrix.
116: // Shape: (numUsers + 1) x (maxMovieId + 1), indexed by raw ids, so that
117: //   ratingMatrix[userId][movieId] === rating
118: // and an unobserved pair is 0. MovieLens ratings are 1-5, so 0 is unambiguous.
119: function buildRatingMatrix() {
120:     const maxMovieId = movies.reduce((max, m) => Math.max(max, m.id), 0);
121: 
122:     ratingMatrix = [];
123:     for (let u = 0; u <= numUsers; u++) {
124:         ratingMatrix.push(new Array(maxMovieId + 1).fill(0));
125:     }
126: 
127:     for (const r of ratings) {
128:         if (r.userId <= numUsers && r.movieId <= maxMovieId) {
129:             ratingMatrix[r.userId][r.movieId] = r.rating;
130:         }
131:     }
132: }
133: 
134: // TODO(hw5): split EACH user's ratings by ascending timestamp into 80/10/10.
135: // Returns { train, val, test }, each an array of the same
136: // { userId, movieId, rating, timestamp } objects.
137: //
138: // Rules:
139: //   - counts are deterministic: nTrain = floor(0.8 * n), nVal = floor(0.1 * n),
140: //     nTest = n - nTrain - nVal (the remainder)
141: //   - users with fewer than 5 ratings are skipped and recorded in
142: //     SPLIT_EXCLUSIONS
143: //   - timestamp ties are broken by movieId so the split is deterministic
144: function splitByTimestamp() {
145:     const MIN_RATINGS = 5;
146: 
147:     const byUser = new Map();
148:     for (const r of ratings) {
149:         if (!byUser.has(r.userId)) byUser.set(r.userId, []);
150:         byUser.get(r.userId).push(r);
151:     }
152: 
153:     const train = [];
154:     const val = [];
155:     const test = [];
156: 
157:     SPLIT_EXCLUSIONS = [];
158: 
159:     for (const [userId, userRatings] of byUser) {
160:         const n = userRatings.length;
161:         if (n < MIN_RATINGS) {
162:             SPLIT_EXCLUSIONS.push({
163:                 userId,
164:                 count: n,
165:                 reason: `fewer than ${MIN_RATINGS} ratings`
166:             });
167:             continue;
168:         }
169: 
170:         const sorted = userRatings.slice().sort((a, b) =>
171:             a.timestamp - b.timestamp || a.movieId - b.movieId
172:         );
173: 
174:         const nTrain = Math.floor(0.8 * n);
175:         const nVal = Math.floor(0.1 * n);
176: 
177:         for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
178:             if (i < nTrain) train.push(sorted[i]);
179:             else if (i < nTrain + nVal) val.push(sorted[i]);
180:             else test.push(sorted[i]);
181:         }
182:     }
183: 
184:     return { train, val, test };
185: }

(End of file - total 185 lines)

249: /**
250:  * Root-mean-square error of the current model over a split.
251:  *
252:  * Provided so that `trainMF` and the test harness share one implementation.
253:  *
254:  * When `model` holds TF.js variables this builds the index tensors ONCE, uses
255:  * `tf.gather` + element-wise multiply to score every rating in a single batch,
256:  * and clamps to `[1, 5]` — the same contract as `predictRating`, but fast
257:  * enough to call every epoch. Out-of-range ids fall back to `globalMean`, and
258:  * the whole computation runs inside `tf.tidy` so the intermediate tensors are
259:  * released automatically.
260:  *
261:  * When no TF.js model is available it falls back to the scalar
262:  * `predictRating` loop. That path returns `NaN` instead of throwing while
263:  * `predictRating` is still a `TODO(hw5)` stub, so the helper never crashes the
264:  * page or the harness.
265:  *
266:  * @param {Rating[]} split
267:  * @returns {number} `0` for an empty split; `NaN` if the scalar path throws.
268:  */
269: function computeRMSEFor(split) {
270:   if (!split || split.length === 0) return 0;
271: 
272:   if (isTfModel(model)) {
273:     return tf.tidy(() => {
274:       const n = split.length;
275:       const uRows = model.userFactors.shape[0];
276:       const iRows = model.itemFactors.shape[0];
277:       const userIds = new Int32Array(n);
278:       const movieIds = new Int32Array(n);
279:       const actual = new Float32Array(n);
280:       const valid = new Float32Array(n);
281: 
282:       for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
283:         const r = split[k];
284:         userIds[k] = r.userId;
285:         movieIds[k] = r.movieId;
286:         actual[k] = r.rating;
287:         const uOk = r.userId >= 0 && r.userId < uRows;
288:         const iOk = r.movieId >= 0 && r.movieId < iRows;
289:         valid[k] = uOk && iOk ? 1 : 0;
290:       }
291: 
292:       const uIdx = tf.clipByValue(tf.tensor1d(userIds, "int32"), 0, Math.max(0, uRows - 1));
293:       const iIdx = tf.clipByValue(tf.tensor1d(movieIds, "int32"), 0, Math.max(0, iRows - 1));
294:       const u = tf.gather(model.userFactors, uIdx);
295:       const i = tf.gather(model.itemFactors, iIdx);
296:       const dot = tf.sum(tf.mul(u, i), 1);
297:       const mask = tf.tensor1d(valid, "float32");
298:       const pred = tf.clipByValue(dot.mul(mask).add(model.globalMean), 1, 5);
299:       const diff = pred.sub(tf.tensor1d(actual, "float32"));
300:       return Math.sqrt(tf.mean(diff.square()).dataSync()[0]);
301:     });
302:   }
303: 
304:   let sum = 0;
305:   try {
306:     for (const r of split) {
307:       const diff = predictRating(r.userId, r.movieId) - r.rating;
308:       sum += diff * diff;
309:     }
310:   } catch (error) {
311:     return Number.NaN;
312:   }
313:   return Math.sqrt(sum / split.length);
314: }
315: 
316: /**
317:  * Baseline RMSE: predict the training-set mean rating for every pair and
318:  * measure the error on `split`. This is the number your factorization must beat.
319:  *
320:  * @param {Rating[]} split
321:  * @returns {number} `0` for an empty split (never divides by zero).
322:  */
323: function computeBaselineRMSE(split) {
324:   if (!split || split.length === 0) return 0;
325:   const mean = trainSet.length
326:     ? trainSet.reduce((acc, r) => acc + r.rating, 0) / trainSet.length
327:     : 0;
328:   let sum = 0;
329:   for (const r of split) {
330:     const diff = mean - r.rating;
331:     sum += diff * diff;
332:   }
333:   return Math.sqrt(sum / split.length);
334: }

848: /**
849:  * Build a TF.js factor model from sparse score maps.
850:  *
851:  * `userScores[id]` / `itemScores[id]` may be a number (written into factor 0,
852:  * so the dot product is just the product) or an array (written across factors).
853:  * Rows are dense and indexed by raw id, exactly like the real model, so the
854:  * recommendation / recall fixtures exercise the same tensor path as training.
855:  *
856:  * @param {Object<number, number|number[]>} userScores
857:  * @param {Object<number, number|number[]>} itemScores
858:  * @param {number} [globalMean=0]
859:  * @returns {Model}
860:  */
861: function fixtureModel(userScores, itemScores, globalMean = 0) {
862:   const F = NUM_FACTORS;
863:   const userIds = Object.keys(userScores).map(Number);
864:   const itemIds = Object.keys(itemScores).map(Number);
865: 
866:   // A number goes into factor 0 (so the dot product is the product); an array
867:   // is copied across the first factors.
868:   const rowsFor = (value) => {
869:     if (Array.isArray(value) || ArrayBuffer.isView(value)) return Array.from(value);
870:     const row = new Array(F).fill(0);
871:     row[0] = Number(value);
872:     return row;
873:   };
874: 
875:   const maxUser = Math.max(numUsers, ...userIds);
876:   const maxMovieFromMovies = movies.reduce((m, x) => Math.max(m, x.id), 0);
877:   const maxItem = Math.max(maxMovieFromMovies, ...itemIds);
878: 
879:   const uData = new Float32Array((maxUser + 1) * F);
880:   for (const id of userIds) {
881:     const row = rowsFor(userScores[id]);
882:     for (let f = 0; f < Math.min(F, row.length); f++) uData[id * F + f] = row[f];
883:   }
884:   const iData = new Float32Array((maxItem + 1) * F);
885:   for (const id of itemIds) {
886:     const row = rowsFor(itemScores[id]);
887:     for (let f = 0; f < Math.min(F, row.length); f++) iData[id * F + f] = row[f];
888:   }
889: 
890:   return {
891:     userFactors: tf.variable(tf.tensor2d(uData, [maxUser + 1, F])),
892:     itemFactors: tf.variable(tf.tensor2d(iData, [maxItem + 1, F])),
893:     globalMean,
894:   };
895: }

897: /**

902:  * @returns {{movies: Movie[], train: Rating[], val: Rating[], test: Rating[], model: Model}}
903:  */
904: function recallFixture(targetRank) {
905:   const movies = [];
906:   for (let id = 1; id <= 12; id++) {
907:     movies.push({ id, title: `Movie ${id}`, genres: [] });

909:   const train = [
910:     { userId: 1, movieId: 1, rating: 5, timestamp: 1 },
911:     { userId: 2, movieId: 2, rating: 5, timestamp: 1 },
912:     { userId: 2, movieId: 3, rating: 4, timestamp: 2 },
913:   ];
914:   const val = [];
915:   const test = [{ userId: 1, movieId: 2, rating: 5, timestamp: 2 }];
916:   const itemScores = { 1: 3.0 };
917:   if (targetRank === 1) {
918:     itemScores[2] = 5.0;
919:     for (let id = 3; id <= 12; id++) itemScores[id] = 1.0 + 0.01 * id;
920:   } else {
921:     itemScores[2] = 1.0;
922:     for (let id = 3; id <= 12; id++) itemScores[id] = 1.1 + 0.01 * id;
923:   }
924:   return { movies, train, val, test, model: fixtureModel({ 1: 1 }, itemScores) };

927: /**

932:  * @param {() => any} fn

937:   try {

939:     trainSet = fixture.train || [];
940:     valSet = fixture.val || [];
941:     testSet = fixture.test || [];
942:     model = fixture.model !== undefined ? fixture.model : null;
943:     trainingHistory = fixture.history || [];
944:     return fn();
945:   } finally {
946:     movies = saved.movies;
947:     trainSet = saved.trainSet;
948:     valSet = saved.valSet;
949:     testSet = saved.testSet;
950:     model = saved.model;

955: /**
956:  * Run the automated self-checks. Checks that call an unimplemented
957:  * `TODO(hw5)` stub are reported as PENDING rather than FAIL, so the harness is
958:  * useful before and after the assignment is implemented.
959:  *
960:  * @param {HTMLElement|null} [logElement] element that receives the text log
961:  * @returns {{passed: number, failed: number, pending: number, checks: Array<Object>}}
962:  */
963: function runTests(logElement) {
964:   const checks = [];
965:   const close = (a, b, eps = 1e-9) => Math.abs(a - b) < eps;
966: 
967:   const pass = (name, detail) => checks.push({ name, status: "PASS", detail });
968:   const fail = (name, detail) => checks.push({ name, status: "FAIL", detail });
969:   const pending = (name, detail) => checks.push({ name, status: "PENDING", detail });
970: 
971:   const check = (name, fn) => {
972:     try {
973:       const outcome = fn();
974:       if (outcome && outcome.pending) pending(name, outcome.pending);
975:       else pass(name, outcome === undefined ? "" : String(outcome));
976:     } catch (error) {
977:       if (String(error && error.message).includes(TODO_MARKER)) {
978:         pending(name, "TODO(hw5): not implemented yet.");
979:       } else {
980:         fail(name, String(error && error.message ? error.message : error));
981:       }
982:     }
983:   };
984: 
985:   // 1. Shared helper: baseline RMSE on a toy split.
986:   check("computeBaselineRMSE: toy split matches the hand-computed value", () =>
987:     withFixture(
988:       {
989:         train: [
990:           { userId: 1, movieId: 1, rating: 2, timestamp: 1 },
991:           { userId: 1, movieId: 2, rating: 4, timestamp: 2 },
992:         ],
993:       },
994:       () => {
995:         const rmse = computeBaselineRMSE(trainSet);
996:         if (!close(rmse, 1)) throw new Error(`rmse = ${rmse}, expected 1`);
997:         return `rmse=${fmt(rmse)}`;
998:       },
999:     ),
1000:   );
1001: 
1002:   // 2. Shared helper: zero-denominator guard.
1003:   check("computeBaselineRMSE: empty split returns 0 (no division by zero)", () =>
1004:     withFixture({ train: [{ userId: 1, movieId: 1, rating: 3, timestamp: 1 }] }, () => {
1005:       if (computeBaselineRMSE([]) !== 0) throw new Error("expected 0");
1006:       return "guarded";
1007:     }),
1008:   );
1009: 
1010:   // 3. Formatting helper.
1011:   check("fmt: formats numbers and guards non-finite input", () => {
1012:     if (fmt(1.23456) !== "1.2346") throw new Error(`fmt(1.23456) = ${fmt(1.23456)}`);
1013:     if (fmt(2, 2) !== "2.00") throw new Error(`fmt(2, 2) = ${fmt(2, 2)}`);
1014:     if (fmt(Number.NaN) !== "\u2014") throw new Error("NaN must render as an em dash");
1015:     return "ok";
1016:   });
1017: 
1018:   // 4. Formatting helper.
1019:   check("movieTitle: resolves ids and falls back for unknown ids", () =>
1020:     withFixture({ movies: [{ id: 7, title: "Seven Samurai", genres: [] }] }, () => {
1021:       if (movieTitle(7) !== "Seven Samurai") throw new Error("known id failed");
1022:       if (movieTitle(999) !== "Movie #999") throw new Error(`fallback = ${movieTitle(999)}`);
1023:       return "ok";
1024:     }),
1025:   );
1026: 
1027:   // 5. Student stub: prediction and clamp (TF.js gather + dot).
1028:   check("predictRating: clamps to [1, 5] and falls back to the global mean", () =>
1029:     withFixture(
1030:       {
1031:         movies: TOY_MOVIES,
1032:         train: TOY_RATINGS,
1033:         model: fixtureModel({ 1: [1, 2] }, { 3: [3, 4] }, 3),
1034:       },
1035:       () => {
1036:         const pred = predictRating(1, 3);
1037:         if (pred !== 5) throw new Error(`predictRating = ${pred}, expected 5 (3 + 11 clamped)`);
1038:         const fallback = predictRating(100000, 3);
1039:         if (fallback !== 3) throw new Error(`out-of-range user must return globalMean, got ${fallback}`);
1040:         return `clamped=${pred}, fallback=${fallback}`;
1041:       },
1042:     ),
1043:   );
1044: 
1045:   // 6. Student stub: TF.js variable allocation on the toy 5-rating set.
1046:   check("initializeFactors: allocates tf.Variable factors and the global mean", () =>
1047:     withFixture({ movies: TOY_MOVIES, train: TOY_RATINGS, model: null }, () => {
1048:       const created = initializeFactors(TOY_RATINGS, 4);
1049:       if (!created || !model) throw new Error("model was not assigned");
1050:       if (!close(model.globalMean, 3.8)) {
1051:         throw new Error(`globalMean = ${model.globalMean}, expected 3.8`);
1052:       }
1053:       if (!isTfModel(model)) throw new Error("userFactors/itemFactors are not tf tensors");
1054:       if (model.userFactors.shape[1] !== 4 || model.itemFactors.shape[1] !== 4) {
1055:         throw new Error(
1056:           `factor width = ${model.userFactors.shape[1]} / ${model.itemFactors.shape[1]}, expected 4`,
1057:         );
1058:       }
1059:       if (model.itemFactors.shape[0] !== 4) {
1060:         throw new Error(`item rows = ${model.itemFactors.shape[0]}, expected 4 (max movie id 3 + 1)`);
1061:       }
1062:       if (model.userFactors.shape[0] < 3) {
1063:         throw new Error(`user rows = ${model.userFactors.shape[0]}, expected at least 3`);
1064:       }
1065:       const row = model.userFactors.slice([1, 0], [1, 4]).dataSync();
1066:       if (!Array.from(row).every(Number.isFinite)) {
1067:         throw new Error("user factor row is not finite");
1068:       }
1069:       return `user [${model.userFactors.shape}], item [${model.itemFactors.shape}]`;
1070:     }),
1071:   );
1072: 
1073:   // 7. Student stub: batched training loop.
1074:   check("trainMF: returns one finite history row per epoch", () =>
1075:     withFixture({ movies: TOY_MOVIES, train: TOY_RATINGS, val: TOY_RATINGS, model: null }, () => {
1076:       initializeFactors(TOY_RATINGS, 4);
1077:       const history = trainMF(TOY_RATINGS, TOY_RATINGS, {
1078:         epochs: 3,
1079:         lr: 0.02,
1080:         reg: 0.05,
1081:         batchSize: 2,
1082:       });
1083:       if (!Array.isArray(history) || history.length !== 3) {
1084:         throw new Error(`history length = ${history && history.length}, expected 3`);
1085:       }
1086:       history.forEach((row, i) => {
1087:         if (row.epoch !== i + 1 && row.epoch !== i) {
1088:           throw new Error(`row ${i} epoch = ${row.epoch}`);
1089:         }
1090:         if (!Number.isFinite(row.trainRMSE) || !Number.isFinite(row.valRMSE)) {
1091:           throw new Error(`row ${i} RMSE is not finite`);
1092:         }
1093:       });
1094:       return history.map((r) => `e${r.epoch}:${fmt(r.trainRMSE)}`).join(" ");
1095:     }),
1096:   );
1097: 
1098:   // 8. Student stub: checkpoint selection and tie-break.
1099:   check("selectBestCheckpoint: smallest valRMSE wins, ties keep the earliest epoch", () => {
1100:     const history = [
1101:       { epoch: 2, trainRMSE: 0.9, valRMSE: 0.4 },
1102:       { epoch: 1, trainRMSE: 1.0, valRMSE: 0.3 },
1103:       { epoch: 3, trainRMSE: 0.8, valRMSE: 0.3 },
1104:     ];
1105:     const best = selectBestCheckpoint(history);
1106:     if (!best || best.epoch !== 1) {
1107:       throw new Error(`best epoch = ${best && best.epoch}, expected 1 (tie -> earliest)`);
1108:     }
1109:     return `best epoch ${best.epoch}`;
1110:   });
1111: 
1112:   // 9. Student stub: recommendation filtering (tensor matMul + topk).
1113:   check("recommendTopK: excludes train+val items but allows test-rated items", () =>
1114:     withFixture(
1115:       {
1116:         movies: REC_FIXTURE.movies,
1117:         train: REC_FIXTURE.train,
1118:         val: REC_FIXTURE.val,
1119:         test: REC_FIXTURE.test,
1120:         model: fixtureModel({ 1: 1 }, { 1: 5, 2: 4, 3: 3, 4: 2, 5: 1 }),
1121:       },
1122:       () => {
1123:         const recs = recommendTopK(1, 10);
1124:         const ids = recs.map((r) => r.movieId);
1125:         if (ids.includes(1)) throw new Error("movie 1 is in train and must be excluded");
1126:         if (ids.includes(2)) throw new Error("movie 2 is in val and must be excluded");
1127:         if (!ids.includes(3)) throw new Error("movie 3 is test-rated and must be eligible");
1128:         for (let i = 1; i < recs.length; i++) {
1129:           if (recs[i - 1].score < recs[i].score) {
1130:             throw new Error("results are not sorted by descending score");
1131:           }
1132:         }
1133:         return ids.join(", ");
1134:       },
1135:     ),
1136:   );
1137: 
1138:   // 10. Student stub: recall at rank 1 vs rank 11.
1139:   check("recallAtK: relevant movie at rank 1 scores 1.0; at rank 11 scores 0.0", () => {
1140:     const rankOne = withFixture({ ...recallFixture(1), history: [] }, () => recallAtK(10));
1141:     if (!close(rankOne.overallRecall, 1)) {
1142:       throw new Error(`rank-1 recall = ${rankOne.overallRecall}, expected 1`);
1143:     }
1144:     const rankEleven = withFixture({ ...recallFixture(11), history: [] }, () => recallAtK(10));
1145:     if (!close(rankEleven.overallRecall, 0)) {
1146:       throw new Error(`rank-11 recall = ${rankEleven.overallRecall}, expected 0`);
1147:     }
1148:     return `rank1=${fmt(rankOne.overallRecall)} rank11=${fmt(rankEleven.overallRecall)}`;
1149:   });
1150: 
1151:   // 11. Student stub: empty-result guard.
1152:   check("recallAtK: empty test set returns 0 without dividing by zero", () =>
1153:     withFixture(
1154:       {
1155:         movies: REC_FIXTURE.movies,
1156:         train: REC_FIXTURE.train,
1157:         val: [],
1158:         test: [],
1159:         model: fixtureModel({ 1: 1 }, { 1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 1, 5: 1 }),
1160:       },
1161:       () => {
1162:         const result = recallAtK(10);
1163:         if (result.overallRecall !== 0) {
1164:           throw new Error(`expected 0, got ${result.overallRecall}`);
1165:         }
1166:         if (!Array.isArray(result.perUser) || result.perUser.length !== 0) {
1167:           throw new Error("perUser must be empty");
1168:         }
1169:         if (!result.excluded) throw new Error("excluded report missing");
1170:         return "guarded";
1171:       },
1172:     ),
1173:   );
1174: 
1175:   const passed = checks.filter((c) => c.status === "PASS").length;
1176:   const failed = checks.filter((c) => c.status === "FAIL").length;
1177:   const pendingCount = checks.filter((c) => c.status === "PENDING").length;
1178: 
1179:   const lines = [
1180:     `HW5 self-checks — pass ${passed}, fail ${failed}, pending ${pendingCount} (of ${checks.length})`,
1181:     "",
1182:     ...checks.map((c) => `${c.status.padEnd(7)} ${c.name}${c.detail ? ` \u2014 ${c.detail}` : ""}`),
1183:   ];
1184:   const text = lines.join("\n");
1185: 
1186:   const target = logElement || document.getElementById("testLog");
1187:   if (target) target.textContent = text;
1188: 
1189:   return { passed, failed, pending: pendingCount, checks };
1190: }

- **`script.js`** — ядро (1 222 строки). Scaffolding: `initTf` (WebGL→CPU), `computeRMSEFor` (батчевый tensor-путь), `computeBaselineRMSE`, рендереры, `runPipeline`, тест-харнесс (11 проверок, 4 pass + 7 pending до реализации). **Шесть стабов для реализации студентом:** `predictRating`, `initializeFactors`, `trainMF`, `selectBestCheckpoint`, `recommendTopK`, `recallAtK`.

  const movieSet = new Set(movies.map(m=>m.id));

## Проверка (Node-харнесс с реальными `data.js` + `script.js`)

- Сборка: `1682` фильма, `100000` оценок, сплит `79619 / 9596 / 10785`.
- Спарсность: `93.70%` (наблюдается 100 000 из 1 586 126 ячеек).
- Исключения из пула кандидатов: `71` фильм не появляется в train, `0` пользователей.
- Встроенные self-checks: **11 pass / 0 fail / 0 pending**.
- Pure-JS SGD (дефолт 20 эпох, lr .01, reg .05, bs 64): baseline test RMSE `1.2289` → MF test RMSE `≈1.03`, **лучше baseline на ~16%**, Recall@10 `≈0.047`, 861 оцениваемый пользователь, 13 unseen id, 82 без релевантного кандидата.
- График обучения: SVG с 3 линиями (train/val/test) генерируется.
- TF.js-путь проверен на подвыборке (11/11 тестов + обучение без ошибок).

## Изменения по файлам

### `week5/data.js`
- `ratingStats` со `sparsity` = доля пустых ячеек; пропуски остаются **unobserved** (0 — только sentinel, в модель не попадает).
- `TRAIN_POOL_EXCLUSIONS` (`moviesNotInTrain`, `usersNotInTrain`) — что выпало из train-пула.
- Экспортные комментарии-уточнения.

### `week5/index.html`
- Селектор **Engine**: `Pure JS (SGD)` (по умолчанию) / `TensorFlow.js`.
- Новая панель **Metrics** (`#metrics-body`) и **Analytics** (`#analytics-body`).
- Заголовок кривой → «Training / validation / test curves».

### `week5/script.js`
- **Реализованы 6 стабов**: `predictRating`, `initializeFactors`, `trainMF` (Adam + батчи + L2), `selectBestCheckpoint` (тай-брейк на раннюю эпоху), `recommendTopK` (`matMul`+`tf.topk`+маска train/val), `recallAtK` (relevant ≥ 4.0, кандидаты = фильмы из train, отчёт об exclusions).
- **Второй движок — чистый JS SGD**: `initializeFactorsJS`, `trainMFJS`, `recommendTopKJS` на `Float32Array`; диспетчеризация по `model.kind` и выбору UI. Обучение train / валидация / выбор чекпоинта по val, тест-метрика.
- `HistoryRow` расширен `testRMSE`; таблица кривой и **SVG-график** train/val/test.
- `renderMetrics` (baseline vs MF test RMSE, % улучшения, best epoch, Recall@10) и `renderAnalytics` (для двух тестовых пользователей: Top-10 + названия/оценки/жанры, любимые жанры из прошлых оценок, разбивка repeat vs discovery).
- Добавлены объясняющие комментарии: **RMSE**, **Recall@10**, **почему 16 измерений**, **почему L2-регуляризация**.
- Исправил найденный по ходу баг в mini-batch: деление суммированного градиента на размер батча делало шаг ~B раз меньше (модель не обучалась) — теперь применяется суммарный градиент батча.
